refuted: FR-213's 'focused input shows a lifted border' is unimplemented, not merely unauthored-and-flagged. app/kudos/new/_components/link-dialog.tsx:120 and :146 apply `outline-none` to both link-text-input and link-url-input with no `focus:`/`focus-visible:` class anywhere in the file (grep for `focus:` in this file returns zero matches) and no matching rule in app/globals.css. This both fails the explicit FR and removes the browser's native focus ring with nothing put in its place — a WCAG 2.4.7 regression on top of the missed acceptance criterion. design/momorph-node-values.md itself calls this value out as unauthored and says to 'flag in code'; the code does neither cite nor flag it, it silently omits it.
reachableRegressions:
The dialog traps pointer events (full-screen overlay) but not keyboard focus, so the range captured for insertLink can go stale against a body the user edited while the dialog was still open. Concretely: LinkDialog is the last focusable region in DOM order after body-editor's textarea (MentionMenu renders `null` while closed per mention-menu.tsx:35, and body-hint is a non-focusable

), and use-dismiss-on-outside.ts only listens for `pointerdown`-outside and `Escape` — it never traps Tab. So Shift+Tab from the just-focused link-text-input (use-body-editor-controller.ts's onOpenLinkDialog focuses it via link-dialog.tsx:69) lands the user back on the live `body-editor` textarea while the dialog is still rendered on top. From there the user can edit `state.body.text` through the ordinary onChange path, tab forward again, fill the dialog fields, and click Lưu: onConfirmLink (use-body-editor-controller.ts:155-157) splices `insertLink` (rich-text.ts:91-96) using `linkRangeRef.current` — captured BEFORE the edit — against the NEW, already-mutated text, with no bounds check against the current text length. Because JS string `.slice()` never throws on an out-of-range index, this doesn't crash; it silently places the link mark at a start/end pair that may no longer correspond to any real span of the post-edit text (worst case: the body shrank below `range.end`, so the mark's declared offsets sit past the actual inserted text and the link silently fails to render at all, or renders over the wrong words) — a data-integrity defect with no error surfaced to the user, reachable through ordinary keyboard navigation and not covered by ID-61..68 (none of which test a body edit between open and confirm, or Tab order at all).

findings.summary: linkRangeRef is captured once at dialog-open and never re-validated at confirm time, and nothing prevents the user from returning focus to the live body-editor textarea while the dialog is open (no focus trap in link-dialog.tsx or use-dismiss-on-outside.ts — only pointerdown-outside and Escape are handled). A body edit between open and confirm makes insertLink (rich-text.ts:91-96) splice a stale range into new text with no bounds check, silently mis-placing or losing the link mark. Fix: either (a) add a focus trap while `open` — a keydown handler in link-dialog.tsx that cycles Tab among the dialog's own focusable children (or render via a native <dialog> element with `showModal()`, which traps focus for free) — or (b) at minimum, in onConfirmLink, re-clamp `linkRangeRef.current` to `[0, state.body.text.length]` and treat a range that no longer matches (e.g. re-derive against a text-length snapshot taken at open) as invalid, falling back to caret-at-end rather than silently misplacing the mark.

FR-213 explicitly requires the focused input to show a lifted border ('Focus: Hiện viền nổi'), and design/momorph-node-values.md instructs flagging it in code since the exact color isn't specified. Neither happened: `outline-none` is applied to both link-text-input (:120) and link-url-input (:146) with no `focus:`/`focus-visible:` replacement anywhere in the file, and no fallback in app/globals.css. This is a missed, explicit acceptance criterion and a WCAG focus-visibility regression, not just an unauthored-and-disclosed value. Fix: add e.g. `focus:border-2 focus:border-[#998C5F]` (reusing the row's own border color) or a `focus-visible:shadow-[...]` 'lifted' treatment to both inputs, with a one-line comment citing this is an unauthored value per momorph-node-values.md.

ID-67 (and the whole suite — confirmed by grep, no test in this file ever intercepts a network request or reads back a submitted payload) only asserts `bodyValue.toContain(validText)`, i.e. that the plain text appears in the textarea. It does not, and structurally cannot given the suite's architecture, prove the acceptance criterion's other half: 'payload gửi đi chứa run { type: "link", text, href }'. A regression that reduced insertLink to plain string concatenation (dropping the link mark entirely) would still pass ID-67. The wiring is verified correct by direct source read (compose-state.ts:98-99 -> rich-text.ts:91-96), so this is a coverage gap rather than a known defect, but it should be tracked: e.g. a future phase could add a doc-level assertion by submitting the kudos and reading the persisted/rendered link back through F004's read path.

insertLink drops any mark that straddles a zero-width (caret) insertion point entirely, whereas insertMention (rich-text.ts:81-88) extends such a mark instead. Verified this is NOT a bug: insertLink's caret case is algebraically identical to what remapMarks (rich-text.ts:99-113) would compute for the same text diff (prefixLen/oldChangeEnd both equal the caret position when nothing is deleted), so insertLink correctly reuses remapMarks' stated 'drop, never re-anchor' policy rather than insertMention's older, more lenient one. Worth a one-line comment noting the deliberate divergence from insertMention so a future reader doesn't 'fix' it into an inconsistency.
